body_markdown:
Base44 has attracted attention as an AI-powered app builder since Wix acquired it in June 2025. For builders who want to create and launch full-stack apps using their existing Claude or ChatGPT workflows, Floot offers managed database, authentication, and hosting infrastructure without requiring separate backend setup.


According to[Google's guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics) , server-side rendering and pre-rendering can make website content easier for search crawlers to access because not all crawlers execute JavaScript.


Whether you already pay for Claude or ChatGPT, need stronger SEO, or want to[build a mobile app](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) without separate development tools, the right choice depends on your requirements. This guide examines seven Base44 alternatives for non-technical founders, freelancers, and small business owners shipping real applications.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **AI billing models vary significantly** : Floot avoids separate AI build-credit charges by connecting to existing Claude or ChatGPT subscriptions for connector-based building, while Floot plan, hosting, and optional AI feature charges remain separate.
- **Managed backend services** : Floot provides[managed PostgreSQL](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) , authentication, serverless endpoints, and file storage without requiring users to configure separate backend services.
- **SEO implementation affects discoverability** : Floot supports server-side pre-rendering, page metadata controls, and[sitemap generation](https://floot.com/docs/projects/seo) , helping crawlers access public app content.
- **Publishing stays under your control** : Floot keeps code changes in preview until you publish, then makes the published version available through its Floot.app address or connected custom domains.
- **Pricing structures affect budgeting** : Floot's[pricing plans](https://floot.com/en/pricing) include daily building-action limits, with failed actions excluded. Optional AI features may cost extra, and hosting beyond the included allowance uses prepaid credits.


## **What to Compare in Base44 Alternatives**


Base44 provides AI-powered app building with integrated databases and authentication. Comparing alternatives involves more than generating an initial app: pricing, workflow compatibility, and ongoing deployment all matter. For a direct comparison of the two app-building approaches, see this[Floot comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-base44-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) .


- **Pricing models** : Base44 tracks message credits and integration credits separately. Its plans have separate monthly allowances for message credits and integration credits.
- **User feedback** : Review independent accounts of debugging, credit consumption, and customer support alongside each platform's documented policies
- **Workflow preferences** : Teams already using Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, or Cursor may prefer a platform compatible with their existing assistants. Actual building capabilities depend on each client's permissions
- **Production requirements** : Evaluate SEO capabilities, custom domains, scheduled tasks, hosting allowances, and deployment options for customer-facing apps


## **1. Floot**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. The connected AI assistant handles development while Floot provides managed infrastructure; available building capabilities depend on the client's connector permissions. Floot is free to start and also offers an optional in-editor AI agent that uses separate Floot AI credits.


### **Core Architecture**


Floot supports three build paths:


- **MCP connector for supported assistants** : Build through Claude, Codex, Cursor, or compatible ChatGPT configurations. When client permissions allow, the assistant creates projects, edits TypeScript/React files, provisions PostgreSQL databases, and returns live previews
- **In-app editor with optional Floot AI agent** : Work inside Floot's browser-based editor with a live preview. The optional Floot AI uses separate AI credits
- **Code editor integration** : Connect Cursor, VS Code, or Zed to Floot's remote MCP server for coding-tool control with managed infrastructure


### **Built-In Services**


Floot includes production backend infrastructure on all plans:


- **Database** : Managed PostgreSQL with SQL access, browser-based table view, and export capabilities. Database compute scales with demand
- **Authentication** : Email/password login plus brokered Google and Microsoft OAuth without separate OAuth app registration
- **File storage** : Managed storage for uploads and assets with CDN-backed delivery for static files
- **Email and notifications** : Transactional email with sent-message logs and web and native mobile push notifications. Sending emails to customers through Floot requires a verified sending domain, which needs a paid plan.
- **Scheduled tasks** : Cron job execution for daily reports, data syncing, and cleanup operations (repeating jobs require a paid plan and a published app)


### **SEO and Search Visibility**


Floot provides[SEO controls](https://floot.com/docs/projects/seo) that support production app requirements:


- Server-side pre-rendering so crawlers receive page-specific HTML, titles, descriptions, and content when enabled
- Page metadata settings for customizing how pages appear in search results
- Support for sitemap.xml and robots.txt through your AI assistant
- Visitor analytics for tracking traffic patterns, with dashboard access on paid plans
- Primary domain and redirect settings


### **Mobile App Conversion**


Floot packages web apps into installable native iOS and Android shells without requiring a Mac or Xcode. The[mobile app builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) work on all plans:


- Free: 2 mobile builds per month
- Pro: 12 mobile builds per month
- Power: Unlimited mobile builds


Builds can connect to TestFlight and Google Play testing tracks, though connecting Google Play requires a paid Floot plan. Final store submission requires separate Apple and Google developer accounts and remains subject to each store's review process.


### **Pricing Structure**


- **Free** : $0/month, 100 build actions per day, with no additional weekly usage pool, 3,000 one-time starter AI credits, a one-time $3 hosting credit at signup, and 2 mobile builds per month
- **Pro** : $25/month (or annual with two months free) with 1,000 daily actions, 5,000 monthly AI credits, $10/month hosting allowance, 12 mobile builds, and custom domains
- **Power** : $100/month (or annual with two months free) with 5,000 daily actions, 15,000 monthly AI credits, $25/month hosting allowance, and unlimited mobile builds


[Pricing and plan](https://floot.com/en/pricing) allowances are as of October 2026 and may change during 2027. Failed actions do not count against building-action limits. Hosting beyond the included allowance uses prepaid credit, with optional auto-reload. For complete plan allowances, credits, and hosting details, see Floot's[billing FAQs](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/billing-credits-and-plans) .


### **Best Use Cases**


Floot works well for builders who:


- Already use Claude, Codex, Cursor, or a compatible ChatGPT configuration and want to leverage that workflow
- Need production SEO capabilities for content-driven or discovery-dependent apps
- Want web and mobile deployment without separate development platforms
- Prefer building through familiar AI assistants rather than learning new interfaces
- Require managed PostgreSQL, authentication, and serverless backends without infrastructure management


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable is a prompt-to-app builder with its own AI chat interface for generating full-stack applications. The platform focuses on generating visual interfaces through a built-in chat workflow.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Built-in AI chat** : Describe your app in natural language, and Lovable's AI generates the frontend and backend code
- **Visual generation** : Creates UI components through natural-language prompts
- **Supabase-style backend** : Integrated database, authentication, and backend services
- **GitHub synchronization** : GitHub code synchronization is available on all plans, while direct codebase downloads require a paid plan
- **Workspace sharing** : Collaboration features for teams


### **App Building Considerations**


The platform suits builders who prefer a self-contained environment with integrated AI and prioritize visual quality in generated interfaces.


### **Organizational Fit**


Lovable offers a Free plan with 5 daily build credits, capped at 30 per month, plus 20 monthly Cloud credits. The Pro plan costs $25/month and includes 100 monthly credits, custom domains, and code mode. Business costs $50/month and adds features such as SSO and additional workspace controls. Annual billing options may offer lower effective monthly rates.


## **3. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new is a browser-based AI app generator from StackBlitz that lets users edit full-stack code directly in the browser. Its Bolt Cloud services provide integrated backend capabilities.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Browser-based IDE** : Full-stack code editing without local setup
- **Bolt Cloud** : Integrated database, authentication, and hosting services
- **Direct code access** : View and modify generated code in real-time
- **Fast initial prototyping** : Quick path from prompt to working demo


### **App Building Considerations**


The platform suits builders who want browser-based code editing without local development setup and prefer direct access to generated code for manual modifications.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bolt.new offers a Free plan with a limit of 300,000 tokens per day and 1 million tokens per month. Its Pro plan costs $25/month when billed monthly and starts at 10 million tokens per month without a daily limit. Pro also includes custom domains, additional database capacity, and unused token rollover. Annual billing is available at discounted rates.


## **4. Replit**


Replit is a cloud IDE with AI-assisted coding capabilities. The platform supports multiple programming languages and provides a full development environment with terminal access.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Multi-language support** : Python, JavaScript, Go, and many other languages
- **Terminal access** : Full command-line environment in the browser
- **AI Agent** : Built-in AI assistant for code generation and modification
- **Real-time collaboration** : Team features for shared development
- **Integrated hosting** : Deploy directly from the development environment


### **App Building Considerations**


The platform suits builders who need terminal access and multi-language support beyond TypeScript/React, plan to hand off projects to developers who want a full IDE, and have development experience.


### **Organizational Fit**


Replit offers a free Starter plan with limited AI-assisted development capabilities. Replit Core costs $20/month, or $18/month billed annually, and includes $20 in monthly usage credits and unlimited workspaces. Replit Pro costs $100/month, or $90/month billed annually, with $100 in monthly usage credits, additional agent capacity, and expanded collaboration features.


## **5. Bubble**


Bubble is a visual app builder with workflow tooling, plugins, and workload-based pricing. Bubble combines its visual editor with AI-assisted app-building capabilities.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Visual editor** : Drag-and-drop interface for designing app layouts
- **Workflow automation** : Built-in logic builder for app functionality
- **Plugin ecosystem** : Marketplace of extensions and integrations
- **Database management** : Visual database editor with relational data support
- **Established platform** : Longer track record with mature documentation


### **App Building Considerations**


Bubble suits builders who prefer visual editing combined with AI assistance, need complex no-code SaaS functionality with extensive customization, want a mature platform with documentation and community, and are comfortable with workload-based pricing that scales with app usage.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bubble offers a Free plan for building and testing applications. For web-only projects billed monthly, Starter costs $39/month, Growth costs $134/month, and Team costs $399/month. Higher tiers provide additional workload capacity, collaboration tools, and deployment features. Bubble also offers separate pricing for mobile-only and combined web-and-mobile applications, with discounts available for annual billing.


## **6. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets users create, host, and share websites and lightweight applications directly through ChatGPT. It supports interactive experiences, persistent data, and access controls, making it a relevant Base44 alternative for people who already use ChatGPT.


### **Primary Focus**


- **ChatGPT-native building** : Create and refine sites through natural language prompts without a separate builder interface
- **Built-in hosting** : Publish websites and supported apps using ChatGPT's Sites workflow
- **Persistent data** : Store application records and uploaded files within supported limits
- **Access controls** : Share sites publicly, privately, or with workspace members, depending on plan permissions


### **App Building Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites suits builders who already use ChatGPT and want to publish directly from it, need lightweight interactive websites, dashboards, or internal tools, prefer ChatGPT's native publishing experience, and have requirements that fit the supported Sites runtime.


For applications needing a separately managed full-stack environment, Floot offers managed Postgres, authentication, Stripe payments, hosting, and mobile publishing workflows through its connector for compatible AI assistants such as Codex, Claude, and Cursor.[ChatGPT integration](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) is also available, although its available actions depend on the ChatGPT workflow.


### **Organizational Fit**


ChatGPT Sites is available on eligible ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise plans, subject to workspace permissions. Building and editing Sites count toward Codex usage, while hosting, traffic, and storage have separate limits. Sites hosting is currently included with Plus and Pro, while Enterprise hosting charges are currently waived. Availability and publishing permissions depend on the applicable plan and workspace settings.


## **7. v0**


v0 is an AI-powered development platform from Vercel that generates interfaces and applications from natural language prompts. It supports frontend development and full-stack projects, with deployment through Vercel.


### **Primary Focus**


- **AI-generated interfaces** : Create React components and application layouts through prompts
- **Full-stack development** : Build applications with frontend and backend functionality
- **Code access** : Review and refine generated application code
- **Vercel deployment** : Publish applications through Vercel's hosting platform


### **App Building Considerations**


v0 suits builders who want AI-assisted interface and application development, prefer working within the Vercel ecosystem, need access to generated code for further customization, and are comfortable managing the services and configuration their application requires. Floot takes a different approach by providing[managed app infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs) that works with existing AI coding assistants.


### **Organizational Fit**


v0 offers a Free plan with $5 in one-time credits for new users and a limit of 7 messages per day. The Plus plan costs $30 per user/month and includes $30 in monthly credits, while Business costs $100 per user/month with $30 in monthly credits and additional data controls. Paid plans also provide daily login credits, with additional credits available for purchase when needed.


## **Why Floot Stands Out as the Top Base44 Alternative**


Floot is a full-stack app-building platform with an[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) for Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. The connected assistant handles development within its permissions, while Floot manages hosting and infrastructure. Connector-based building uses your existing AI service, with Floot action limits, hosting, and optional AI credits accounted for separately.


Floot provides managed PostgreSQL, authentication, storage, payments, email, and scheduled jobs on paid plans.[Published apps](https://floot.com/docs/projects/publishing) run on Floot.app subdomains, with custom domains available on paid plans. Optional server-side pre-rendering helps crawlers access page content and metadata, while live previews let you check updates before publishing.


Floot handles[native app builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) without requiring a Mac or Xcode. The Free plan includes 2 mobile app builds per month, Pro includes 12, and Power includes unlimited builds. Google Play connection requires a paid Floot plan; app store releases still require developer accounts and approval. See[Floot pricing](https://floot.com/en/pricing) for current plan allowances.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the main difference between Floot and Base44?**


Floot uses a "bring your own AI" model through supported assistants such as Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations, while Base44 bundles its own AI with platform-specific credits. Connector-based building does not add separate Floot AI build-credit charges, but Floot plans, hosting, and optional AI features have their own costs. Building and editing permissions depend on the connected client. Floot also provides SEO controls and mobile app builds on all plans.


### **Can I move an existing Base44 project to Floot?**


Floot cannot import an existing Base44 codebase directly, as its[import documentation](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) explains. However, you can use your existing app as a reference and ask your AI assistant to rebuild its functionality through Floot's connector. Floot provides the managed database, authentication, and hosting, although existing code, data, and integrations may require manual adaptation.


### **How does Floot handle payments and Stripe integration?**


Floot provides built-in Stripe payment processing for one-time payments and subscriptions. Your AI assistant can set up checkout flows and test transactions in the preview without connecting a Stripe account. Accepting real payments requires a Pro or Power plan and your own Stripe account, with applicable Stripe processing fees and a Floot payment fee of 1% on Pro or 0% on Power. Floot's built-in[payment setup](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/payments) handles standard checkout and subscription workflows without requiring manual Stripe API keys or webhook configuration.


### **Is Floot suitable for non-technical founders?**


Yes. Floot targets non-technical founders building MVPs, small business owners needing custom internal tools, and entrepreneurs validating product ideas. The platform handles database provisioning, authentication setup, and deployment automatically. You describe what you want in natural language to a supported assistant, and, when its connector permissions allow building, the assistant uses Floot's managed infrastructure without requiring you to write code directly.


### **Does Floot support custom domains and professional hosting?**


Custom domains require a paid plan (Pro or Power). Floot provides managed hosting with CDN-backed asset delivery, and database compute scales with demand. Pro plans include a $10/month hosting allowance, while Power plans include $25/month. Usage beyond the allowance is billed against prepaid credit with optional auto-reload. Primary domain settings and redirects support professional deployment configurations.
